You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:
cond   vavg V  vmax V  vpp mV   tup s  Pload uW  vout_min vout_max ripple   startup  settled 
S1       2.24    2.25    26.2   0.269      15.2  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       ok       ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 4 of 12.

RESULTS OF YOUR PREVIOUS ROUND:

Design 1 'SSHI_Hybrid_Sync': failed the screen and was not tuned (topology 547c528cb3d2).

BEST DESIGNS SO FAR (values already tuned):

reply.reasoning:
*   Goal: Power sensor-node RL from a storage capacitor at node `out`.
    *   Constraints:
        *   `vout_min`: vavg >= 1.8 V
        *   `vout_max`: vmax <= 3.6 V
        *   `ripple`: vpp <= 0.05 V (0.7-0.8s)
        *   `startup`: tup <= 0.4 s
        *   `settled`: dv <= 0.02 V
    *   Best Design: `SSHI_FullBridge` (score 77.06, 5/6 conditions passed).
    *   Failing for S2 (Heavy Load):
        *   `ripple`: 0.074 V (needs <= 0.05 V)
        *   `settled`: 0.079 V (needs <= 0.02 V)
    *   Wait, S2 (RL = 150 kOhm) is the heavy load. The `vavg` is high (3.28 V), but the ripple and the stability (`dv`) are the issues. This suggests that the storage capacitor `C1` might be too small for the heavy load, causing larger voltage swings, or the rectifier/SSHI combo is creating a ripple that exceeds the limit.
    *   `C1` is currently 1.8 uF.

    *   The SSHI_FullBridge topology uses a Full-Bridge Rectifier (FBR) combined with a synchronous switch and inductor for L-Cp inversion.
    *   Current Components:
        *   FBR (D1, D2, D3, D4)
        *   L1 (inductor)
        *   S1 (switch controlled by G1)
        *   C1 (output capacitor)
        *   DZ1 (zener clamp)
        *   G1 (SYNC controller)
    *   The failing condition is specifically on the ripple and settling for S2.
    *   S2 is the heaviest load (150 kOhm).
    *   Wait, if `vavg` is 3.28 V and RL is 150 kOhm, $P_{load} = V^2/RL = 3.28^2 / 150,000 \approx 71.7 \mu\text{W}$.
    *   The ripple is 74 mV, and $dv$ is 79 mV.
    *   Usually, ripple $\Delta V \approx I_{load} \cdot \frac{T}{C}$.
    *   For S2: $I_{load} = 3.28\text{V} / 150\text{k}\Omega = 21.8 \mu\text{A}$. $T = 1/100\text{Hz} = 10\text{ms}$.
    *   Estimated ripple $\Delta V = 21.8\mu\text{A} \cdot 10\text{ms} / 1.8\mu\text{F} \approx 0.12\text{mV}$.
    *   The observed ripple (74 mV) is much higher than this simple estimate. This implies the ripple is coming from the switching action or the charging pulses, not just the discharge between peaks.

    *   The `SSHI_FullBridge` uses a full bridge rectifier. This is a standard approach.
    *   The L-Cp inversion part (L1, S1) is designed to flip the charge on the piezo capacitor to increase efficiency.
    *   If the ripple is too high, we might need a larger `C1` (but the optimizer already tried sizing it up to 4.7 uF) or a better way to smooth the output.
    *   However, the `S2 settled` failure ($dv = 0.079\text{V}$) suggests the output voltage is drifting or oscillating. Since it's a passive storage capacitor, a drift usually means the power balance ($P_{in}$ vs $P_{out}$) is not quite stable yet or is changing.

    *   Wait, let's look at the `vavg` of `SSHI_FullBridge`. It's around 3.3-3.4 V for most cases.
    *   The Zener clamp `DZ1` is at 3.3 V.
    *   For S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, the `vavg` is very close to the Zener voltage (3.3 V).
    *   When the voltage hits the Zener limit, it clamps. This might be causing the "settling" issue (dv) because the voltage is fighting the Zener clamp and the load.
    *   If we want a more stable voltage below 3.6 V, we could:
        1.  Increase the Zener voltage (but we only have `DZ33`).
        2.  Use a different topology that doesn't rely on a Zener clamp for the maximum voltage, or one that naturally settles lower.
        3.  Increase `C1` further (already limited by 4.7 uF).

    *   Wait, the `SSHI_FullBridge` is almost there. Only S2 fails on ripple and settling.
    *   Actually, if `vavg` is 3.3V and `vmax` is 3.31V for S2, the ripple is 74mV. This means the voltage is oscillating around the Zener clamp.
    *   The Zener `DZ33` starts conducting around 3.3 V. If the energy harvester is trying to push the voltage to 3.5 V and the Zener is pulling it down to 3.3 V, we get a balance.

    *   The current `SSHI_FullBridge` is:
        Piezo -> L1 -> S1 -> (Full Bridge) -> C1.
        Wait, the provided topology says:
        D1 pzp out, D2 pzn out, D3 0 pzp, D4 0 pzn. (This is a Full Bridge Rectifier).
        L1 pzp n1, S1 n1 pzn. (This is the L-Cp inversion circuit).
    *   This structure is a bit odd. Usually, in SSHI, the L-S circuit is in parallel with the piezo to flip the voltage, and *then* it's rectified.
    *   In `SSHI_FullBridge`:
        - The FBR is connected directly to pzp and pzn.
        - The L-S circuit is also connected to pzp and pzn (via n1).
        - This means the FBR is drawing current from the piezo, AND the L-S circuit is flipping the piezo voltage.
    *   Since it's a full bridge, the voltage at `out` is $\max(V_{pzp}, V_{pzn}, 0)$.
    *   The L-S circuit flips $V_{pzp}$ and $V_{pzn}$.

    *   Is there a way to reduce ripple for the heavy load?
    *   A larger capacitor `C1` is the obvious answer. If the optimizer already tried 4.7 uF and it still failed, we need a different topology.
    *   Wait, looking at the results: `S2 vavg 3.28, vmax 3.31, vpp 74.2mV`.
    *   If `vmax` is 3.31 and `vavg` is 3.28, and the ripple is 74 mV, the voltage is swinging between roughly 3.24 and 3.32. This is very tight.

    *   Let's try a Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) variant.
    *   SECE typically uses a switch to connect the piezo to the rectifier only at the peaks.
    *   Standard SECE:
        Piezo (pzp, pzn) -> Switch (S1) -> Rectifier -> C1.
    *   Wait, the goal is to be efficient and stable. Let's try a modified SSHI or a more robust SECE.

    *   Let's try a "Parallel-SSHI" or a different rectifier.
    *   Actually, the "Standard" SSHI (Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor) usually has the L-S flip and then a *half-bridge* (one diode) because the flipping makes the voltage always positive (or negative) relative to ground.
    *   But a Full Bridge is more robust.

    *   What if we use a larger `C1` value in the proposal to guide the optimizer? The current `C1` is 1.8 uF. The max is 4.7 uF.
    *   What if we remove the Zener and use a different mechanism to limit voltage? But we only have Zener. If we remove the Zener, `vmax` might exceed 3.6 V in S3.
    *   In S3, `vavg` is 3.4 V and `vmax` is 3.41 V with the Zener. Without the Zener, it would likely shoot up.

    *   Let's try a "Charge Pump" or "Voltage Doubler" approach? No, that's for low voltages.
    *   How about a "Synchronous Rectifier" using the switches?
        We have 4 switches max.
        We could use 2 switches for the rectifier and 1 for the flip.
    *   But `SYNC` controllers are limited to 2.

    *   Let's try a "Buck-Boost" or "Boost" type? No, too complex for 16 components and 2 SYNCs.

    *   Let's try an "improved" SECE:
        The piezo is connected to a switch S1, which then goes to a diode D1, then to `out`.
        Another switch S2 connects pzn to ground? No.
        Actually, a simple SECE:
        S1: pzp -> n1 (ctrl G1)
        D1: n1 -> out
        S2: pzn -> n2 (ctrl G1)
        D2: n2 -> out
        This would extract charge at the peaks.

    *   Wait, look at the `SSHI_FullBridge` again. It's almost perfect.
    *   The failure is `S2 ripple` and `S2 settled`.
    *   S2 is RL = 150 kOhm.
    *   If `vavg` is 3.28 V and RL is 150 kOhm, the load current is 21.8 uA.
    *   The ripple is $vpp = 74\text{mV}$.
    *   Is it possible that the `ton` of the SYNC is too long, causing huge current spikes that ripple through the capacitor?
    *   `ton` is 19.6 us.
    *   L is 1.79 mH. Cp is 25 nF.
    *   $\pi \sqrt{L \cdot C_p} = 3.14 \cdot \sqrt{1.79\text{e-3} \cdot 25\text{e-9}} = 3.14 \cdot 6.69\text{e-6} = 21 \mu\text{s}$.
    *   The `ton` (19.6 us) is very close to the ideal.

    *   What if we use a slightly different topology to see if it's more stable?
    *   Maybe a "Half-Bridge SSHI"?
        D1: pzp -> out
        S1: pzp -> n1 (ctrl G1), L1: n1 -> pzn.
        Wait, this is for when the piezo is grounded.

    *   Let's try a "Synchronous Rectifier" (SR) using switches instead of diodes for the main path.
        S1: pzp -> out (ctrl G1)
        S2: pzn -> out (ctrl G2)
        This would eliminate the diode drop and possibly reduce the ripple.
        But we need the L-Cp flip.

    *   Let's try an "SSHI with a larger C1" and a slightly different bridge.
        Actually, let's try a "Parallel SSHI" where the L-S circuit is separate from the rectifier.
        The `SSHI_FullBridge` already does this.

    *   What if we change the Zener to a different configuration or replace it with a RC filter? No, we need the clamp.

    *   Let's try a "Buck-like" output? No.

    *   Wait! I have an idea. The ripple on S2 is caused by the load being heavy.
        If we can increase the energy harvested, we might be able to use a larger `C1` and still have `tup` be okay.
        But `vavg` is already 3.28 V, which is very high (near the limit).
        If we can't increase `vavg`, the only way to reduce ripple is `C1`.
        Is it possible the optimizer didn't find the best `C1` for S2 because it was optimizing for other conditions?
        The `C1` value 1.8 uF was tuned. Maybe 4.7 uF would work for S2 ripple but fail `tup`?
        For S2: `tup` is not reported (meaning it might be too slow).
        Wait, for S2 in `SSHI_FullBridge`, `tup` is not listed!
        "cond vavg vmax vpp tup... S2 3.28 3.31 74.2 - 71.6 ok ok FAIL ok FAIL"
        Actually, the table shows `tup` is missing for S2. If `tup` is missing, it means `V(out)` never reached 1.8 V? No, `vavg` is 3.28 V.
        If `vavg` is 3.28 V and `tup` is missing, it means the simulation ended before it hit 1.8 V? No, it's 0.8 s.
        Wait, "missing if never". If `vavg` is 3.28 V, it must have passed 1.8 V.
        Let me re-read: "tup = first time V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never)".
        If `vavg` is 3.28 V, it definitely reached 1.8 V. Why is it missing?
        Wait, look at the table again:
        `S1 3.37 3.38 25.2 0.157 34.3 ok ok ok ok ok`
        `S2 3.28 3.31 74.2 - 71.6 ok ok FAIL ok FAIL`
        Wait, the `tup` column is the 4th one. For S2, it is `-`.
        This is very strange. How can `vavg` be 3.28 V and `tup` be missing?
        Ah, maybe it reached 1.8 V *after* 0.4 s?
        "startup: tup <= 0.4 s".
        If `tup` is 0.45 s, it is "FAIL".
        So for S2, the startup is too slow.

    *   To fix startup (tup) and ripple (vpp) for S2:
        1.  Increase `C1` to reduce ripple (but this makes `tup` slower!).
        2.  Increase the energy harvested per cycle to make `tup` faster.
        3.  Wait, the `vavg` is already 3.28 V. We are harvesting plenty of power. The problem is the *rate* of charging at the start.

    *   If we use a smaller `C1`, `tup` is faster, but `vpp` is higher.
    *   If we use a larger `C1`, `tup` is slower, but `vpp` is lower.
    *   We need a way to have both.
    *   This is a classic trade-off. How to break it?
        - Use a "fast-charge" path?
        - Use a more efficient extraction?

    *   Wait, what if we use a "half-bridge" rectifier for the SSHI flip?
        In a typical SSHI:
        The L-S circuit flips the piezo voltage.
        The piezo is then connected to `out` via a single diode.
        This only works if the piezo is grounded on one side.

    *   Let's try a "Dual-Inductor" or "Boosted" approach.
        Actually, let's try a simpler approach first.
        Maybe the Full Bridge is overkill and the diode drops are hurting the startup?
        DSCH has a 0.25 V drop. In a full bridge, you have 2 diodes in series. That's 0.5 V.
        If we can use a single diode (Half-Bridge), we save 0.25 V.

    *   Let's try a "Half-Bridge SSHI":
        - S1: pzn -> 0 (ctrl G1) -- this grounds the piezo.
        - L1: pzp -> n1, S2: n1 -> 0 (ctrl G1) -- this flips the charge on Cp.
        - D1: pzp -> out.
        Wait, the SYNC controller only gives us 2 SYNCs.
        This is getting complex.

    *   Let's try a "SECE" again, but properly.
        S1: pzp -> n1 (ctrl G1)
        D1: n1 -> out
        S2: pzn -> n2 (ctrl G2)
        D2: n2 -> out
        Wait, this is just a synchronous rectifier.

    *   What if we try a "Capacitive" SSHI? No.

    *   Let's go back to the `SSHI_FullBridge` and try to optimize it.
        Wait, I can't optimize values, only topology.
        Is there a topology that's more efficient than `SSHI_FullBridge`?
        The current `SSHI_FullBridge` has:
        L1, S1 (flip) + D1, D2, D3, D4 (rectify).
        Maybe we can replace the full bridge with something more efficient?
        Like a "Synchronous Rectifier" (using switches).
        But we only have 2 SYNCs.
        G1 is used for the flip. G2 could be used for the rectification.
        S2: pzp -> out (ctrl G2, edges=pos)
        S3: pzn -> out (ctrl G2, edges=neg)
        But we still need the flip.
        S1: n1 -> pzn (ctrl G1)
        L1: pzp -> n1.

    *   Wait, if we use S2 and S3 for rectification, we don't need D1-D4.
        This would eliminate the 0.5 V drop!
        Let's try this:
        L1: pzp -> n1
        S1: n1 -> pzn (ctrl G1) -- the flip
        S2: pzp -> out (ctrl G2) -- the rectification (pos)
        S3: pzn -> out (ctrl G2) -- the rectification (neg)
        C1: out -> 0
        DZ1: 0 -> out

        Wait, if S2 and S3 are controlled by G2, we need to make sure they don't short the output to ground.
        G2: edges="both", but we need to know when to close which.
        S2 (pzp->out) should close when pzp is at its peak positive.
        S3 (pzn->out) should close when pzn is at its peak positive (which is when pzp is at its peak negative).
        This is exactly what a Full Bridge does, but with switches.

        Let's refine this:
        L1: pzp -> n1
        S1: n1 -> pzn (ctrl G1, edges="both") -- flip
        S2: pzp -> out (ctrl G2, edges="pos") -- rect pos
        S3: pzn -> out (ctrl G2, edges="neg") -- rect neg
        C1: out -> 0
        DZ1: 0 -> out
        Wait, the SYNC `edges` can be "both", "pos", or "neg".
        But G2 can only have one `edges` setting.
        If G2 is "both", both S2 and S3 will close at the same time, shorting pzp to pzn!
        So we need TWO different SYNCs for S2 and S3.
        G2: edges="pos", S2: pzp -> out
        G3: edges="neg", S3: pzn -> out
        But we are limited to 2 SYNCs total!
